text.BHSA 2CH 34:7: וַיְנַתֵּ֣ץ אֶת־הַֽמִּזְבְּחֹ֗ות וְאֶת־הָאֲשֵׁרִ֤ים וְהַפְּסִלִים֙ כִּתַּ֣ת לְהֵדַ֔ק וְכָל־הַֽחַמָּנִ֥ים גִּדַּ֖ע בְּכָל־אֶ֣רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּ֖שָׁב לִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ ס
text.KJV 2CH 34:7: And when he had broken down the altars and the groves, and had beaten the graven images into powder, and cut down all the idols throughout all the land of Israel, he returned to Jerusalem.
text.BHSA 2CH 34:8: וּבִשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁמֹונֶ֤ה עֶשְׂרֵה֙ לְמָלְכֹ֔ו לְטַהֵ֥ר הָאָ֖רֶץ וְהַבָּ֑יִת שָׁ֠לַח אֶת־שָׁפָ֨ן בֶּן־אֲצַלְיָ֜הוּ וְאֶת־מַעֲשֵׂיָ֣הוּ שַׂר־הָעִ֗יר וְ֠אֵת יֹואָ֤ח בֶּן־יֹֽואָחָז֙ הַמַּזְכִּ֔יר לְחַזֵּ֕ק אֶת־בֵּ֖ית יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽיו׃
text.KJV 2CH 34:8: Now in the eighteenth year of his reign, when he had purged the land, and the house, he sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah, and Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah the son of Joahaz the recorder, to repair the house of the LORD his God.
text.BHSA 2CH 34:9: וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ אֶל־חִלְקִיָּ֣הוּ׀ הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּדֹ֗ול וַֽיִּתְּנוּ֮ אֶת־הַכֶּסֶף֮ הַמּוּבָ֣א בֵית־אֱלֹהִים֒ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָסְפֽוּ־הַלְוִיִּם֩ שֹׁמְרֵ֨י הַסַּ֜ף מִיַּ֧ד מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה וְאֶפְרַ֗יִם וּמִכֹּל֙ שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּמִכָּל־יְהוּדָ֖ה וּבִנְיָמִ֑ן וישׁבי יְרֽוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
text.KJV 2CH 34:9: And when they came to Hilkiah the high priest, they delivered the money that was brought into the house of God, which the Levites that kept the doors had gathered of the hand of Manasseh and Ephraim, and of all the remnant of Israel, and of all Judah and Benjamin; and they returned to Jerusalem.

A.name: Shaphan
A.notes: He was sent to repair the house of the Lord (2CH 34:8)
family: scribe-of josiah (Josiah, prophesied son of the house of David (1KI 13:2), King of Jud)
grandfather-of gedaliah (Gedaliah, son of Ahikam, appointed King of Judah by Nebuchadnezzar (2K)

B.name: Shaphan
B.line: Secretary/scribe of King Josiah who read the found law-book to him.
family: companion-of hilkiah-2 (Hilkiah, the high priest of King Josiah's reign (2KI 22:4, 2CH 34:9))
scribe-of josiah (Josiah, prophesied son of the house of David (1KI 13:2), King of Jud)

why: The Hebrew names one Shaphan, son of Azaliah, sent to repair the temple, matching A’s stated event. However, B has the same father and serves the same king, so the supplied facts do not distinguish the records; the verse does not name two different Shaphans.
